rationale: Re-verified 2026-10-10 structurally rather than by intent, and the previously recorded blocker was WRONG. What holds: the advisory is a crash in the Prometheus exporter's HTTP listener, @opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus appears zero times in app/yarn.lock, and the sdk-node 0.46.0 entry there depends on core, resources, sdk-metrics and sdk-trace-base/node pinned at 1.19.0 and on no prometheus exporter at all, so the vulnerable module is absent from the installed graph and the listener cannot be constructed; the wiring this copy serves (server/packages/domain-events-infra/src/Infra/OpenTelemetry/OpenTelemetrySDK.ts) supplies an explicit OTLP PeriodicExportingMetricReader instead. What was wrong: the previous entry said the patched 0.217.0 needs @opentelemetry/api >= 1.9 while 0.46.0 pins the peer below 1.8. The registry gives 0.217.0 a peer range of >=1.3.0 <1.10.0 against 0.46.0's >=1.3.0 <1.8.0, and app/yarn.lock holds api 1.7.0 and 1.8.0, so the peer is not a blocker and that reason cannot be relied on. The real blocker is the family: 0.217.0 pins core, resources, sdk-metrics, sdk-trace-base and sdk-trace-node at 2.7.1 and adds @opentelemetry/configuration, while the installed copies are pinned at exactly 1.19.0 by this published dependent and by sdk-trace-node@1.19.0, so a keyed resolution on sdk-node alone puts two OpenTelemetry families underneath one prebuilt published package — and 0.217.0 adds exporter-prometheus as a hard dependency, installing the very module whose absence is today's mitigation. A family migration of a published dependency in the app lock domain, not a resolution.

Re-verified 2026-10-10: the vulnerable JaegerPropagator.extract is only reachable once the propagator is registered, and the telemetry wiring this transitive copy serves (server/packages/domain-events-infra/src/Infra/OpenTelemetry/OpenTelemetrySDK.ts line 61, the source of the published domain-events-infra the bundled home server depends on) passes a single explicit textMapPropagator of AWSXRayPropagator, which replaces the default propagator set rather than adding to it; git grep finds no OTEL_PROPAGATORS value anywhere in the tracked tree except this rationale, so nothing re-adds jaeger. Not resolvable by a pin: the registry shows the patched 2.9.0 depending on @opentelemetry/core 2.9.0, while this copy's dependent sdk-trace-node@1.19.0 pins core 1.19.0, so adopting it crosses OpenTelemetry major families inside a published patched dependency of the app lock domain — a family migration, not a keyed resolution.

Re-verified 2026-10-10 on both sides, from the published package and from the installed one. There is no patched version in this major: the registry lists 2.0.3 and 2.0.4 as the only fixed releases (dist-tag latest 2.0.4, legacy 1.2.1 — and 1.2.1 is itself inside the advisory's >=0.6.3 <=2.0.2 range), so a 1.x floor cannot clear it. And 2.x cannot be adopted: in the packed 2.0.4, dist/cjs/index.d.ts exports only imageSize(input: Uint8Array), while path input moved to the separate subpath export image-size/fromFile as the ASYNC imageSizeFromFile(filePath: string). The installed metro 0.84.4, read out of app/.yarn/cache, calls the default export SYNCHRONOUSLY with a FILE PATH at src/Assets.js lines 174-177 (assetInfo.files[0]; a Buffer only when the asset sits inside a .zip), so a keyed resolution to 2.x breaks that call and even a Metro code change could not keep it synchronous. Metro is repository-controlled mobile bundler tooling that never parses third-party images, and this parser is absent from every shipped application and server runtime. Revisit when Metro adopts fromFile.

Re-verified 2026-10-10: there is still NO patched braces release to move to. npm view braces versions ends at 3.0.3, which is the version installed here, and the advisory covers <=3.0.3, so no resolution, floor or dedupe can clear it and a pin would only relabel the same bytes; app/yarn.lock holds a single copy (braces@npm:^3.0.3, braces@npm:~3.0.2 both resolving to 3.0.3). The single dependent is chokidar 3.6.0, a development-time file watcher used by the bundler and test runners; it expands only glob patterns that this repository authors, never request data, and it is absent from every shipped runtime bundle. The previous entry deliberately kept a one-month horizon so the first published fix would be picked up; two monthly re-checks have now returned the same newest-ever 3.0.3, so the horizon is a quarter instead — re-checking is one npm view, and nothing about the exposure can change until upstream publishes.
